briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have seen a significant escalation in rhetoric and economic pressure against Iran, coupled with continued Israeli military operations. Iran has firmly asserted its "complete and decisive" control over the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to block vessels without coordination, while the US has intensified economic sanctions, labeling them "Operation Economic Outcast" and targeting financial institutions dealing with Iran. Meanwhile, Israel conducted drone strikes in Jenin, killing a Hamas commander and two accomplices, and eliminated two terror operatives in Gaza City, citing ceasefire violations.

IRAN
President Masoud Pezeshkian announced plans to raise the price of non-subsidized fuel to 10,000 Toman (approximately 100,000 Rial) per liter, an increase of 5,000 Toman, citing blocked import routes due to "war conditions." He also reported Iran has sold 90 million barrels of oil since the implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). The IRGC Navy declared "complete and decisive" control over the Strait of Hormuz, stating it would block all vessels attempting transit without coordination with Iran, dismissing US claims of the waterway being open as "obvious lies." President Pezeshkian linked the reopening of Hormuz to the US lifting sanctions, releasing Iranian funds, and forcing Israel to cease attacks on Lebanon. Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran would not compromise on its security, asserting that "our fighters will respond to any fire with greater fire." Araghchi emphasized strong diplomatic defense of national interests and claimed victory in both the "40-day war" and subsequent three-month negotiations. Intelligence forces arrested six members of the "Jaish al-Zolm" terrorist group in Saravan, killing one during the operation. Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement calling for national unity, social cohesion, economic resilience through domestic production, and phasing out the US dollar, while implicitly criticizing officials who "frankly express weaknesses," calling it a "great help to the enemy." President Pezeshkian is scheduled to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on September 1, 2026. Economically, Iran faces significant challenges, with the Statistical Center reporting an 89% year-on-year inflation rate in August and the Central Bank reporting 84.4% in July, alongside high food inflation (oil up 258%, food up 128%). Domestic reports detail widespread public hardship, including low wages for teachers and military personnel, rising student fees, high unemployment, and agricultural sector distress due to low prices, diesel shortages, and electricity cuts.

ISRAEL
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) carried out a drone strike in Jenin, West Bank, killing three Palestinian terror operatives, including Qais Bitawi, identified as the head of Hamas's activities in the Jenin refugee camp, along with two accomplices. The IDF stated Bitawi was actively planning "significant terror activities" and had ties to Hamas in Gaza. This marks a rare occurrence of Israeli airstrikes in the West Bank since early 2025. In Gaza City, the IDF confirmed two separate strikes killed Ibrahim Nabil Ibrahim Bass, a Hamas commander who participated in the October 7, 2023, attack, and Hamdi Ahmad Hamid Kahlil, an Islamic Jihad surveillance platoon commander. The IDF justified these strikes, stating the operatives had "systematically violated the ceasefire" by advancing attacks and restoring terror group capabilities. Politically, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urged Ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich to unite for the upcoming elections, but Ben Gvir rejected a joint run with Smotrich. Smotrich is reportedly in advanced talks with Moshe Feiglin's "Zehut" party for a technical bloc. Israeli police and Shin Bet indicted two northern residents suspected of pledging allegiance to ISIS and planning an attack on the Temple Mount.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In addition to the Jenin strike mentioned above, Palestinian media reported three fatalities from an Israeli strike near al-Qarara, close to Khan Younis, though the IDF initially denied strikes in the area this morning. Civil defense teams in Gaza recovered 233 bodies and remains from under rubble, with 174 still missing, following Israeli occupation forces' actions. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers were documented vandalizing Palestinian farmlands in Burqa village, east of Ramallah.

LEBANON
Israeli airstrikes targeted several locations in southern Lebanon, including Al-Mansouri, Ali Al-Taher heights, Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, and Kafr Roummane, accompanied by artillery shelling and machine-gun fire, which Press TV described as ceasefire violations. Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem reiterated the resistance fighters' sacrifices as a defense of their rights and future, claiming that US and Israel are facing growing economic, political, and international losses. Qassem asserted that Iran is the leading force countering US-Israeli hegemony and that Hezbollah will not be defeated, having "broken the project of 'Greater Israel'." Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi met with the Vice President of Lebanon's Supreme Islamic Shia Council (SISC), Sheikh Ali Khatib.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, violent armed clashes and a loss of security control were reported in Jdeidet Artouz, Rif Dimashq, between local residents and individuals from Deir Ezzor province. In Iraq, the US administration plans to end military aid to Kurdish Peshmerga forces when the current agreement expires on September 30. NATO officials stated that the mission in Iraq has no defined end date, but its team was temporarily relocated to Italy in March due to security conditions. A fire erupted at a Popular Mobilization Units (PMU) headquarters at Camp Speicher in Salah al-Din province.

GULF STATES
Reuters reported that Gulf states are accelerating investments in ports, pipelines, and railways to reduce their reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, in response to months of disruption from the Iran-Iraq conflict. Yemen's Ansarullah movement launched drone attacks against Saudi mercenaries in the city of Al-Mokha. A high-ranking Ansarullah official advised Saudi authorities to "reconsider their calculations" regarding Yemen. The US Treasury imposed severe financial restrictions on branches of the Egyptian bank Banque Misr in the UAE due to their dealings with Iran, cutting their access to US banking services as part of "Operation Economic Outcast."

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iran's Hormuz Stance**: IRGC Navy declared "complete and decisive" control over the Strait of Hormuz, vowing to block all non-coordinated vessels, while President Pezeshkian conditioned reopening on US lifting sanctions and halting Israeli actions in Lebanon.
2.  **US Sanctions on Iran**: The US Treasury launched "Operation Economic Outcast," imposing strict financial restrictions on Banque Misr branches in the UAE for ties to Iran, cutting off access to US banking services and dollar transactions.
3.  **Jenin Drone Strike**: An Israeli drone strike in Jenin killed three Palestinian terror operatives, including Qais Bitawi, identified as the head of Hamas's Jenin refugee camp activities, and two accomplices.
4.  **Gaza Terror Operatives Eliminated**: The IDF killed two high-ranking terror operatives in separate strikes in Gaza City: Ibrahim Nabil Ibrahim Bass (Hamas commander involved in Oct 7 attack) and Hamdi Ahmad Hamid Kahlil (Islamic Jihad surveillance commander).
5.  **Iran's Domestic Economic Strain**: President Pezeshkian announced a significant fuel price hike and acknowledged war-related import route blockages, while official reports showed high inflation (84.4% to 89% y/y) and public hardship.
6.  **Hezbollah's Resolve**: Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem affirmed Hezbollah's unwavering stance against US-Israeli "hegemony" in the region, stating they "will not be defeated" and have broken the "Greater Israel" project.
7.  **Gulf States Bypass Hormuz**: Gulf nations are reportedly increasing investments in alternative trade routes (ports, pipelines, railways) to mitigate reliance on the Strait of Hormuz.
8.  **US-Venezuela Oil Deal**: President Trump announced the "largest oil deal in world history" with Venezuela, securing US control over significant oil reserves without taxpayer cost.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain extremely high, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's assertive control claims directly contradict US declarations of an open waterway. The US sanctions on entities dealing with Iran further tighten economic pressure, potentially provoking more aggressive Iranian responses beyond rhetorical threats. Active flashpoints include the West Bank (Jenin, settler activity) and southern Lebanon, where Israeli strikes and Hezbollah's firm rhetoric maintain a volatile environment. Iran's internal economic distress and leadership statements about "war conditions" suggest a high domestic sensitivity to external pressures, potentially influencing risk calculations. The reported shifting of Israeli military assets underground indicates concern over Iran's missile capabilities.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: President Trump announced a "historic" oil deal with Venezuela, securing over 65 billion barrels of oil reserves for the US without taxpayer cost. Secretary of State Marco Rubio hailed it as a "huge victory." The US Treasury initiated "Operation Economic Outcast," imposing strict financial restrictions on Banque Misr branches in the UAE for transactions with Iran, preventing their access to US banking services. CIA Director John Ratcliffe undertook a secret diplomatic mission to Moscow, reportedly asking Russia not to share intelligence with Iran and reinforcing US commitment to NATO's Article 5. Trump asserted that the Strait of Hormuz is "open" and that Iran's response to US actions has been "very limited," also claiming that US divers had cleared mines from the Strait. He further asserted "ownership" of the Strait. US media reported a transfer of large quantities of ammunition to the Middle East to counter Iran.
**Russia**: President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to meet Iranian President Pezeshkian on September 1, 2026. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov indicated that Moscow opposes transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz but acknowledged Iran's demand for sanctions relief in exchange for keeping the Strait open, stating "they will do it."
**Gulf States**: Some Gulf states are accelerating investments in ports, pipelines, and railways to reduce their strategic dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.
**Pakistan**: Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar discussed Iran-US tensions with senior UK officials, noting that the UK praised Pakistan's diplomatic mediation efforts.
**International Organizations**: The UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO) reported approximately 6,000 seafarers on 400 ships are still unable to leave the Persian Gulf due to the Strait of Hormuz closure. The World Food Program warned of choke points at Hormuz, Bab al-Mandeb, and the Black Sea.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictory Claims**: There are direct contradictions regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz. US officials, including President Trump and CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper, state the Strait is "open" and mines have been cleared, while the IRGC Navy asserts "complete and decisive" control, threatening to block vessels without coordination. The UN IMO reports 6,000 seafarers stranded in the Persian Gulf, supporting the notion of restricted passage.
**Unverified Claims**: Iranian internal sources (mamlekate, kianmeli1) claim Iran is redirecting fuel to Russia due to Russia's shortages and that fuel is being exported while Iranians face domestic queues, which remains unverified by official sources. Kianmeli1 also reports a missile and drone launch from Sirik towards Hormuz, which is not corroborated elsewhere. There are persistent unverified claims from US media personality David Vance and even President Trump about Mojtaba Khamenei being "killed" or "severely injured"; Mojtaba Khamenei's recent written statement suggests he is alive, though his lack of public appearances is noted.
**Propaganda Indicators**: Statements from Iranian and US officials regarding the Strait of Hormuz and economic sanctions contain strong propaganda elements, with each side portraying its actions as justified and the other's as illegal or delusional. The Iranian Foreign Ministry's strong condemnation of US sanctions as "international crime against humanity" and "state terrorism" is highly charged language aimed at international delegitimization. Trump's "largest oil deal in world history" claim and his "no longer Mr. Nice Guy" message are typical of his populist rhetoric.
**Reporting Gaps**: While Iran attributes its fuel shortages to blocked import routes and "war conditions," specific details on which routes are blocked or by whom are not provided. The full humanitarian scope of the Israeli strikes and Palestinian casualties in Gaza is difficult to ascertain from the provided fragmented reports. The nature and targets of Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon are reported broadly (towns, heights) without further specifics on damage or casualties, other than "violation of ceasefire." The details of the alleged ISIS plot in Israel and the heavy fighting in Syria's Jdeidet Artouz are also sparse.
